title: “They Say in the School of Rav”
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.6) they said that wherever it says “they say in the school of Rav,” it is Rav Huna; and it is objected: “But did not Rav Huna say, ‘They say in the school of Rav’? Rather (it is) Rav Hamnuna.” Hyman considers both attributions correct and reconstructs the history as follows. When Rav died, the academy of Sura remained without a head out of respect for Shmuel, who remained the teacher of the whole Diaspora in Nehardea, and all of Rav’s great students came to study before Shmuel. But the academy of Sura was not abolished, and there was there a gathering of sages whose leader was Rav Hamnuna, as explained in his entry, and they sent all their doubts to Shmuel, as we find in [Gittin 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.66b.5) and 89a, [Bava Batra 152b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.152b.8), [Sanhedrin 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.24b.14) and [Shevuot 46a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.46a.2): “They sent from the school of Rav to Shmuel: Let our master teach us.” And when the students stated a halakhah in Rav’s name, it was said — [Shabbat 85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.85a.4), [Eruvin 89b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.89b.2-3) and [Eruvin 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.94b.3), [Yevamot 83a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83a.4) — “They say in the school of Rav in Rav’s name”; and Hyman considers that this was certainly said by Rav’s great students, such as Rav Huna, who reigned after Shmuel’s death. Hyman cites Berakhot 3a for Rav Ada bar Ahavah reporting a teaching from Rav’s school. He counts Rav Ada among Rav’s great students.[^4] But we also find in [Zevachim 87a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.87a.2), “They say in the school of Rav: What is Rav Chisda’s reason?” and there the reference is to the study house.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman reconciles the Huna/Hamnuna attributions through his academy-history reconstruction; this is not a global formula-to-person binding. His certainly assertion and the later generic study-house sense remain attributed and distinct.

Sanhedrin 17b directly gives the Huna proposal, objection and Hamnuna answer. The subsequent reconciliation through Sura’s academy history and the certainty attached to Rav’s senior students are Hyman’s reconstruction, not a universal assignment of the formula to one person.

Sanhedrin answers Rav Hamnuna after objecting to Rav Huna, while Yevamot 83b does use the expression for Rav Huna. The letters sent to Shmuel and the rulings transmitted in Rav’s name are separate formulas. Heilprin gives the concise Hamnuna identification. See also [Yevamot 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83b.5). See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=598&lang=en).

Rav Ada bar Ahavah uses the formula “they say in the school of Rav” at [Sanhedrin 74b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.74b.10) and [Makkot 23b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Makkot.23b.4). The two occurrences introduce different teachings. The wording is unverified at Hyman’s supplied Berakhot 3a.
